result:
I reviewed only the Task 10 fence surface (fence, its grant reservation, broker wiring, tools, git bootstrap, and the two fence test files) as data. Below is the report; I've also written it to the plan file.

## Summary

The core invariants largely hold: capture-before-yield, single-call grant/permit binding, identity revalidation inside a synchronous critical section, create-only publication via `linkSync`, revision-checked replacement, and reverse-order removal of captured identities only. I found **no way for the model to obtain a write outside its declared, granted paths** — the escalation attempts I traced all fail closed (`grant_escalation` / `filesystem_alias` / `grant_mismatch`).

The actionable gaps are correctness, error-typing, bookkeeping, and coverage.

---

### F1 — HIGH: `birthtimeNs` identity is not portable; the fence invalidates its own captures on Linux
`filesystem-mutation-fence.ts:66` (`birth: stat.birthtimeNs`), compared at `:73`.

libuv fills `birthtim` from `st_ctim` on Linux (Node documents the ctime fallback). Every native call the fence itself makes updates ctime of the object **and of its parent directory**: `mkdirSync` (`:199`), `linkSync` (`:265`, `:332`), `renameSync` (`:258`), `unlinkSync`/`rmdirSync` (`:318`, `:336`). The very next `current()` — `:200`, `:260`, `:267`, `:320`, `:335`, `:337`, `:354` — then compares a stale `birth` and fails `filesystem_identity_changed` **after the effect has already landed**.

Repro: run the existing test `"ordinary create, revision replacement, patch, directory move and recursive delete work"` (`test/filesystem-mutation-fence.test.ts:189`) on Linux/ext4. Expect: `fs.write` with `createDirectories` fails (mkdir bumps the workspace dir's ctime→birth), and the recursive delete fails mid-tree with files already gone.

Minimal fix: probe once whether the platform exposes a real birthtime (create a temp file, `chmod`, compare `birthtimeNs`); when it does not, make `same()` compare `dev+ino+directory` only. Do **not** simply refresh identities after each mutation for parents — that would erase the parent-substitution detection that `test:92` relies on.

Acceptance: **block** until a Linux run is green (or the product is explicitly declared Windows-only in the fence header).

---

### F2 — MEDIUM-HIGH: untranslated errno escapes the typed contract and leaves the ledger in-doubt
`filesystem-mutation-fence.ts:203-213` (`translate`) maps only EEXIST/ENOENT/ENOTEMPTY/EXDEV/ENOTSUP/EOPNOTSUPP/ENOSYS. `EPERM`, `EACCES`, `EBUSY`, `EMLINK`, `EROFS`, `ENOSPC`, `EISDIR`, `ENOTDIR`, `ELOOP` fall through `default: return error`. `filesystemMutationFailure` (`:359-360`) then returns `undefined`, `tool-broker.ts:470-475` rethrows **without** `completeLedger`, while `settleToolBudget` already ran (`:469`). The next identical call gets `in_doubt` → `reconciliation_required` even though nothing was mutated.

Most likely trigger on the stated Windows host: another process holds the destination open without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, so `fs.renameSync` (`:258`) fails `EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EBUSY` — exactly the scenario the comment at `:253-255` claims was empirically tested. Second trigger: `linkSync` (`:265`, `:332`) is `EPERM` on FAT/exFAT and some SMB mounts, so **create and move are unusable there with an untyped error**.

Repro: Windows helper process opens `value.txt` with `dwShareMode=0`, then invoke `fs.write` with the correct sha256.

Minimal fix: add `case "EPERM": case "EACCES": case "EBUSY": case "ETXTBSY":` → a typed refusal (e.g. reuse `filesystem_identity_changed` semantics or add `filesystem_mutation_blocked`), plus a `default:` wrap into a typed code so nothing untyped ever leaves the seam; and call `completeLedger` on every refusal path.

---

### F3 — MEDIUM: destructive approval is never bound at the seam; `fs.move` isn't marked destructive
`execution-grants.ts:151-152` returns only `workspacePath`/`access`/`externalApproved`, so `fencedDelete` (`:322`) and directory `fencedMove` (`:339`) cannot and do not check `destructiveApproved`. Separately `filesystem-tools.ts:392-398` omits `destructive: true` for `fs.move` although it unlinks the entire source tree (`:336`, `:357`).

Repro: `permissionProfile: "project"`, recording `approve` callback; `fs.move` a directory → no approval request, whole source tree removed; the equivalent `fs.delete` would have prompted.

Minimal fix: return `destructiveApproved` from `reserveExecutionGrantForFilesystemMutation`, require it in `fencedDelete` and in the directory branch of `fencedMove`, and set `destructive: true` on `fs.move`'s `assessAccess`.

---

### F4 — MEDIUM: partial progress is counted and thrown away
`record.effects` is incremented at `:200, :259, :266, :320, :333, :337, :354` and **never read anywhere**. A recursive delete/move that fails midway (`ENOTEMPTY`, identity change, F2 errno) throws a single typed error with no indication that N objects were already deleted or moved. The requirement explicitly allows partial progress *reporting*; today the model is told only "identity changed".

Repro: 3-file directory; inject a new file into a subdirectory after `preflightTree` (`:309`) via the existing `beforeExecute` hook + a mocked `fs.rmdirSync`; observe two files gone and a bare `filesystem_identity_changed`.

Minimal fix: track `completed: string[]` (workspace-relative) on `Authorized`, include `{ effects, completed }` in `error.details` for `fs.delete`/`fs.move`, and surface it in `filesystemMutationFailure` (`:371`).

---

### F5 — MEDIUM: temp-file leak when ownership can't be established
`publish` `:246-248`: `fd = fs.openSync(temporary, "wx", ...)` succeeds, then `owned = identity(fs.fstatSync(fd, ...))`. If `identity()` throws (`ino === 0n` on some SMB/FUSE/network mounts, `:64`), `owned` stays `undefined`, the `finally` guard at `:272` skips cleanup, and `.aiboard-<uuid>.tmp` is left in the user's workspace. It is also not covered by `DEFAULT_IGNORE_BLOCK` (`git-baseline.ts:22-37`), so the next baseline commits it.

Minimal fix: set `created = true` immediately after `openSync`, drive the `finally` from `created` (verifying via the open `fd`'s `fstat` rather than a fresh `lstat`), and add `.aiboard-*.tmp` to the bootstrap ignore block.

---

### F6 — MEDIUM: a non-canonical workspace root disables all mutations (reads keep working)
`canonical()` (`:80-82`) requires `realpathSync.native(component) === resolve(component)` for **every ancestor including the volume root**, and `authorizeFilesystemMutation:144` requires `reservation.workspacePath` (realpath'd, `execution-grants.ts:524`) to equal `captured.workspace` (only `resolve`d, `tool-broker.ts:117`).

Repro (Windows): `subst X: C:\repos`; construct the broker with `X:\ws`. Every mutation fails `filesystem_alias`/`grant_mismatch`; `fs.read`/`fs.list` still work. Same on macOS via `/var`→`/private/var` (which the fence tests themselves use through `tmpdir()`), and on any junctioned dev folder.

Minimal fix: canonicalize the workspace root once in the `ToolBroker` constructor (reuse `canonicalExistingDirectory`) and anchor capture to that canonical root; keep the per-component realpath check for components *below* the root only.

---

### F7 — LOW-MEDIUM: replacement silently narrows permissions
`:246` passes the captured mode to `openSync`, which applies the umask. `fs.patch` on a `0o664` file under umask `022` yields `0o644`; `0o775` → `0o755`. POSIX ACLs/xattrs and Windows explicit per-file ACLs are also dropped by the temp-write replacement. Fix: `fs.fchmodSync(fd, mode)` after open; document the ACL/xattr limitation next to the non-CAS caveat.

### F8 — LOW-MEDIUM: absolute host paths leak to the model
`filesystemMutationFailure:371-372` emits `error.details` verbatim; `fail()` (`:59-61`) always stores the **absolute** path, and the cleanup error (`:275-277`) adds absolute `temporary` plus `String(cleanup)`. The `revision_conflict` branch carefully relativizes (`:367`) — inconsistent. Fix: relativize/redact `path` and `temporary` in one place before emitting.

### F9 — LOW: unavoidable refusals with no workaround
Any captured tree containing a symlink fails the whole `fs.delete`/`fs.move` (`:63` via `captureTree:108`) — pnpm `node_modules`, many repos. Any hardlinked file fails `hardlink_confinement_unprovable` (`:65`). Trees > 10 000 entries fail (`:104`). Consider allowing lstat-verified `unlink` of symlink *entries* (unlink never follows) and making the error text actionable.

### F10 — LOW: synchronous O(entries × depth) realpath storm
`current()` (`:170-172`) revalidates the full ancestor chain with a `realpathSync.native` per component for **every** tree entry, plus `preflightTree` re-reads every directory. A 10 000-entry delete blocks the event loop. Also `captureFilesystemMutation` walks the whole tree *before* approval (`tool-broker.ts:268`), and `captureTree` recursion is depth-unbounded (`RangeError` → untyped, see F2). Fix: memoize realpath per component per call; cap depth.

### F11 — LOW: approval fidelity
`parents()` (`:194-202`) creates directories that are not in the grant's `access` list and were never shown to the approver; recursive delete removes a whole captured tree while `ToolApprovalRequest.access` shows only the root. Fix: include captured entry count / would-create list in the approval request.

### F12 — LOW: the non-CAS caveat is documented on only one path
The disclaimer at `:157-160` sits on `revalidate`, but `removeExact`'s name-based `unlinkSync`/`rmdirSync` (`:318`), `moveFile`'s `unlinkSync` (`:336`) and `parents`' `mkdirSync` (`:199`) have the same irreducible window, and no portable "unlink-if-inode-matches" exists. Document all four uniformly so nobody later assumes delete is CAS-protected.

---

### Missing test coverage (all actionable)
1. **The claimed Windows empirical result at `:253-255` has no test.** Add: helper process opens the destination with `dwShareMode=0`; assert a *typed* refusal (depends on F2).
2. **"Must not delete unknown objects" is untested.** Add: create a new file inside a captured subdirectory after `preflightTree`; assert `filesystem_identity_changed` and that the new file survives.
3. Partial-progress reporting for recursive delete/move (depends on F4).
4. Untested codes: `directory_not_empty`, `ambiguous_patch`, `filesystem_cleanup_unverified`, Win32 device/ADS rejection (`:86-89`), `hardlink_confinement_unprovable` on the delete/move paths (only the write path is covered at test `:121`).
5. Unknown hardlink appearing **between** capture and mutation (only pre-existing hardlinks are covered).
6. Permit replay into a different call/context — `take()`'s mismatch branches (`:179-183`) are only exercised for same-call double use (test `:155`).
7. Diagnostics consuming the grant must block a later filesystem effect (`reservation.assertCurrent` → `grant_consumed`).
8. Outside-workspace mutation under a non-`full` profile (`externalApproved === false` → `grant_escalation`). The fixture only runs `permissionProfile: "full"`.
9. **No architecture test that this is the *sole* seam.** `tool-broker.ts:267` gates capture purely on the tool *name*; any other native tool importing `node:fs` write APIs bypasses the fence entirely with nothing to detect it. Add a source-scan test.
10. No Linux/macOS matrix (F1, F6).
11. The "junction" tests (`:109`, `:117`, `:138`) silently degrade to plain symlinks on POSIX — add a platform assertion or `t.skip` so the junction case isn't falsely reported as covered.

---

### Acceptance recommendation
**Request changes — do not accept as-is.** Block on F1, F2, F3, and coverage items 1, 2, and 9. F4/F5/F6 should land in the same change or a tracked immediate follow-up. F7–F12 are acceptable as documented follow-ups. The authorized non-CAS residual and its controlled test (`test:173-188`) are correctly scoped and honestly documented — I am not asking for a portable atomic primitive, only that the *detectable* failures above (errno-blocked rename, in-doubt ledger, unbound destructive approval) be refused and typed.
